text: FY25 & 1Q26 results wrap: AI-driven demand remains strong
Mixed FY25 results amid ongoing sector divergence

This report summarizes the 1Q26/FY25 results for fabless & IDM companies under our coverage. A-share semiconductor companies reported mixed FY25 results, with a relatively balanced beat/miss profile and continued divergence across sub-sectors. Sector revenue grew at an average of c.15% YoY in 4Q25, supported primarily by recovery in computing-related demand, while profitability remained volatile. By segment, companies with memory chips exposure (e.g., Montage) delivered strong results, benefiting from DDR5 penetration and product upcycle tailwinds, whereas power semi (NCE, Silan) or vendors with major smartphone exposure (i.e. Goodix, Maxscend) generally reported soft results. H-share listed companies under our coverage reported mixed FY25 results, with Horizon Robotics delivering strong topline growth (+58% YoY). In addition, InnoScience and Black Sesame posted solid FY25 revenue growth at 46% YoY and 73% YoY, respectively, but remained loss-making, reflecting investment phase in emerging segments.
1Q26: clearer recovery momentum, led by AI demand

Encouragingly, 1Q26 marked a clearer acceleration in sector fundamentals, with revenue growth expanding to c.30% YoY on average and earnings growth rebounding more meaningfully. The improvement was primarily volume-driven, reflecting gradual demand recovery and early signs of AI-related demand ramp across computing and AIoT. Within our coverage, Montage and GigaDevice continued to outperform, while AI-related names (e.g., Rockchip) maintained solid growth momentum on product ramp-up and expanding end-market adoption. Overall, we continue to see a stable recovery trend, with AI-exposed and computing-related segments leading, while traditional power semis remain in a more gradual recovery phase.
Preferred stock picks; estimates & PO changes

Considering growth visibility, earnings trajectory and structural positioning, we like Montage for its (1) sustained DDR5 upgrade cycle, (2) ramp-up of PCIe Retimer / other emerging products (e.g., MRCD / MDB), and (3) solid growth of CPU/server shipment. GigaDevice offers solid secular growth, driven by continued share gains in DRAM / MCU / NOR Flash and benefits from memory upcycle. InnoScience is also preferred for promising growth outlook with multiple long-term growth drivers (AIDC, auto, robotics). Horizon Robotics stands out on strong revenue growth and expanding design wins, benefiting from rising ADAS penetration and scaling of its next-generation automotive SoCs. We also see Rockchip and NCE Power as beneficiaries of AIoT and power semi demand recovery, respectively.
We revise our estimates and POs for Montage, Goodix, and Silan.

text: According to BofA Global Memory Tech Team (report on 30 Apr), the memory “supercycle” is expected to continue into 2027-2028. Most chipmakers seem to be expecting sub-20% annual bit growth (for DRAM and NAND) in 2028-30 even with newly constructed fabs.

text: Sales recovery with improving downstream demand

According to WSTS data, global MCU demand has started to recover, with both shipment and ASP trends turning positive since 1Q26, following a prolonged downcycle driven by weakness in automotive and industrial end-markets. The pace of recovery remains gradual but clearly bottomed out.

In contrast, China has seen a stronger and earlier rebound, supported by resilient demand in consumer electronics and policy-driven consumption recovery. China MCU revenue returned to positive growth in early 2026, with March 2026 sales up low teens YoY, indicating improving volume momentum.

text: Promising sales recovery for power semi in 2026E
Global power discrete demand has bottomed since late 2025, with YoY growth turning positive as the cycle recovers from a prolonged downturn.

China continues to outperform, with solid YoY growth in 1Q26 driven by new energy and automotive demand, in our view. We expect further recovery in China to be mainly volume-driven, while pricing may witness recovery for MOSFET from 2Q26E as many power semi companies (including NCE power) raised the price.

China IGBT and MOSFET demand has entered a clear recovery phase since late 2025, with momentum further strengthening into 1Q26. IGBT sales have rebounded more sharply, delivering strong YoY growth, while MOSFET has shown a more gradual but steady recovery (up mid-teens YoY in March 2026), according to SIA data.

We attribute the recovery primarily to volume growth, supported by improving demand in key end-markets such as new energy and industrial applications. Despite the demand rebound, overall pricing remains under pressure amid ongoing competition.

text: Topline recovery but margins under pressure

China power semiconductor companies have shown a clear revenue recovery since 2024, with aggregate sales revenue growth accelerating into 1H25 and remaining solid into 1Q26 (\~20% YoY on average), indicating ongoing demand recovery. However, the growth trajectory has become more moderated since 2H25, suggesting a shift from early-cycle rebound to a more normalized expansion phase.

In contrast, gross margins (GPM) have remained under pressure. On a positive note, we see a modest recovery trend to \~26.6% on average in 1Q26. This trend highlights that the current upcycle is primarily volume-driven, while market competition may remain intensified.

text: Reiterate Buy on Montage as we believe the company provides a unique combination of: 1) broad portfolio of interconnect chips (memory interface chip, PCIe retimer and others) with revenue exposure focusing on servers (both non-AI and AI servers), and 2) TAM expansion opportunities from new products (MRCD/MDB and PCIe switch). In view of better demand outlook for CPU as discussed in recent Intel and AMD results, we think it will be positive for Montage's shipment of memory interface chip ahead. Hence, we raised our FY26-28E net earnings estimates by $3 - 5\%$ . Accordingly, our DCF-based PO is adjusted to RMB251 (from RMB220) based on unchanged WACC of $9.0\%$ and L-T growth rate of $3\%$ . Our new PO implies 57x FY27E P/E, on back of $49\%$ EPS CAGR in FY25-27E.
Better CPU demand outlook driven by agentic AI

AMD recently raised its CY30 server CPU TAM to \$120bn vs. \$60bn prior, on greater emerging agentic AI demand for orchestration CPU (see report). BofA US Semiconductor team recently raised the CPU shipment forecast for AMD & Intel and expect AMD and Intel Server CPU shipment to grow 20% YoY in 2026E on Agentic AI trend. As memory interface chip is used to connect CPU to DRAM within a server, we see positive implications on future memory interface demand.

text: Exhibit 23: We expect Montage to post 35% revenue CAGR in FY25-28E
4Q25 results: solid earnings with softer top-line

Goodix recently reported its 4Q25 & 1Q26 results. 4Q25 revenue reached Rmb1.22bn, up 5% YoY while down 4% QoQ, which is 22% below BofAe estimate. Net profit in 4Q25 increased 3% YoY to Rmb160mn (80% above our estimate). In 1Q26, revenue was down 9% YoY / 20% QoQ to Rmb969mn due to softer demand amid a low season for smartphones, in our view. Despite solid ramps of emerging products (e.g., ultrasonic F/P) through FY25, mgmt. noted that the market's view on end-demand (e.g., smartphones) has turned more cautious amid recent memory pricing hikes. In view of a more muted outlook for industry end-demand, we trim our FY26-27E revenue forecasts by 10-11%. Rolling over valuation, our DCF-based PO is adjusted to Rmb73 (from Rmb89). Reiterate our Neutral rating given balanced risk / rewards in terms of valuation.
FY26E: further ramp-up of new products

In FY25, total revenue recovered 8% YoY to Rmb4.74bn, driven by rapid shipment growth from new products including the ultrasonic F/P sensor, security (NFC/eSE), light sensors and active stylus ICs, per mgmt. The ultrasonic F/P sensor has already surpassed optical and capaCitive F/P sensors in revenue contribution in FY25; mgmt. expects ultrasonic F/P product to account for >40% of fingerprint sensor revenue in FY26E, supported by rising penetration in Android smartphones (from \~10% in 2025 to >20% over the next few years). On R&D, Goodix will focus on OLED TDDI and high-power audio, with OLED TDDI product validation expected in 2026E, according to mgmt.
GPM improvement as rev mix shifting

FY25 GPM improved 0.4ppt YoY to 42.2%, driven by the ramp of new products and better cost economics on existing products following iteration. While upstream foundries are passing through higher fabrication costs, mgmt. believes overall cost remains manageable.

text: FY25: softer topline and earnings; maintain U/P

FY25 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rmb13.05bn (3% below consensus / BofAe), while net profit reached Rmb399mn (up 81% YoY), 32% / 36% below consensus / BofAe. We believe the weaker-than-expected topline and earnings were due to continued pricing pressure on competition and heightened depreciation expenses on capacity expansion. In view of softer-than-expected revenue & earnings growth, we trim our FY26-27E revenue / earnings forecasts by 2-3% / 1-8%. Rolling over valuation, our PO is adjusted to Rmb20.3 (from Rmb18.9) based on 36x 2Q26-1Q27E P/E (from previous FY26E P/E). Maintain our Underperform rating on Silan.
Growth led by Integrated Circuit biz. (e.g., MCUs) in FY25

By revenue segment, in FY25, integrated circuits revenue rose \~20% YoY to c.Rmb4.9bn, driven by continued ramp-up of IPM modules, 32-bit MCUs and automotive-grade analog / power management ICs, per mgmt. IPM modules remained a key growth contributor, with revenue up \~25% YoY to Rmb3.6bn, supported by deeper penetration into inverter-based applications across white goods, industrial and autos. Mgmt. also highlighted strong growth traction in 32-bit MCUs, with revenue up \~55% YoY. Meanwhile, power discrete and modules revenue grew \~17% YoY to Rmb6.4bn, led by robust growth in auto- and solar-related IGBT and SiC products (+40%+ YoY to c.Rmb3.3bn), reflecting ongoing volume ramp in EV main drive and PV inverter applications, in our view.
FY26E: solid rev growth with compressed margins

The GPM slightly declined 0.3ppts to 18.8% in FY25, mainly dragged by higher depreciation from phased capacity ramp-up. Mgmt. indicated that overall capacity utilization reached high levels in FY25, while R&D expenses stayed elevated amid continued investment in autos, SiC and advanced analog platforms. For FY26E, we expect high-teens YoY revenue growth, though margin upside is likely to lag topline in the near term.

text: Our PO of HK\$20 is based on a 50/50 blend of P/S and DCF to reflect near-term growth and long-term outlook. We choose the P/S valuation metric because Black Sesame is rapidly growing its revenue while it is still loss-making, rendering P/E inappropriate. Our P/S based valuation is HK\$20.4, based on 7x 12-mth Fwd P/S. Our multiple of 7x represents a c.60% discount to the market cap weighted average FY26E P/S of major AI / ADAS SoC chip vendors in China, given that the company has a much smaller revenue scale vs. its peers and it is still loss-making with low visibility of break-even in the near term.
Our DCF based valuation is HK\$19.6, applying 10.7% WACC (2.5% risk-free rate, 8% market risk premium, and 1.2x beta), and 3% terminal growth rate. We also assume HKDCNY FX rate at 0.89.

Upside risks: 1) faster-than-expected ADAS/AD penetration in China, 2) better-than-expected sales of new product, 3) better-than-expected progress of customer development, and 4) earlier-than-expected breakeven.
Downside risks: 1) intensified market competition, 2) supply chain disruption, 3) slower customer development progress, and 4) tendency of auto OEMs developing autonomous driving solutions in-house.

Our PO of Rmb455 is based on 40x 2H26-1H27E P/E, which is in-line with the average valuation of Chinese fabless peers with similar margins (memory, MCU and analog). Besides, it is within its historical trading range of c.30-120x 12mth Fwd PE.
Upside risks: (1) better-than-expected DRAM/NAND price hike, (2) better-than-expected margin profiles on faster traction to high-end MCU/NOR markets, and (3) faster ASP recovery of NOR / MCU.

Downside risks: (1) fiercer competition from local peers in MCU/NOR, which may lead to ASP and margin pressure, (2) softer industry demand and (3) slower-than-expected growth from new products, such as LPDDR4 and 3D DRAM.
Our PO of RMB20.3 is based on 36x 2Q26-1Q27E P/E, which is set as the average of China power semi IDM due to similar growth.

Upside risks: (1) better-than-feared price competition from global and local peers (2) faster-progress to high-end market segment including silicon carbide and autos, and (3) higher-than-expected capacity utilization.

Downside risks: (1) slower-than-expected end-demand that translates into headwinds for growth (2) fiercer-than-expected competition from domestic peers, that translates into margin pressure (3) execution risk in ramping up capacity and yield, that translates into slower traction in gaining design wins and product mix upgrade.

Our PO of HK\$11.9 is based on a 50/50 blend of P/S and DCF to reflect near-term growth and long-term outlook. We choose the P/S valuation metric because Horizon Robotics is rapidly growing its revenue while it is still loss-making before breakeven from FY28E, rendering P/E inappropriate. Our P/S based value is HK\$12.0, based on 22x 12-month forward P/S. Our multiple of 22x is in-line with the market cap weighted average P/S of Horizon Robotics' China peers (major AI Chip / ADAS SoC chip vendors) given that we expect the company to post comparable FY25-28E revenue CAGR of 58% vs. peers.
Our DCF based valuation is HK\$11.8, applying 10.7% WACC (2.5% risk-free rate, 8% market risk premium, and 1.2x beta), and 3% terminal growth rate. We also assume HKD/CNY FX rate at 0.89.
Upside risks: 1) more orders win from auto OEM especially the foreign brand, 2) earlier-than-expected roll-out of more advanced solutions (with J6P), 3) earlier-than-expected breakeven.

Downside risks: 1) slower-than-expected ADAS/AD penetration in China, 2) stiff competition, 3) supply chain bottleneck, and 4) a higher proportion of OEMs/ Tier-1 suppliers with in-house solution development.

Our PO of HK\$92 is based on a DCF valuation (WACC: 10.7%, terminal growth: 3%), reflecting positive outlook on InnoScience's long-term growth trajectory. Our PO implies a FY26E price/sales growth (PSG) of 0.4x, based on 89% FY25-27E revenue CAGR. The 0.4x implied PSG is largely in line with peers' average of FY26E PSG.
Upside risks: (1) faster-than-expected GaN adoption in data center and robotics, (2) earlier-than-anticipated profitability, and (3) better customer development progress with more new design wins.
Downside risks: (1) prolonged capex cycles weighing on profitability, (2) intensified competition leads to lower pricing, and (3) execution challenges under an IDM model.

Our PO of Rmb50 is based 7x 12mth forward P/S, taking 30% discount to the average P/S valuation of its A-share peers given weaker profitability. We think P/S is an appropriate valuation metric as the company is loss making in FY26E.

Upside risks: (1) stronger-than-expected recovery of global smartphone shipment, (2) quicker-than-expected revenue ramp-up of advanced modules, and (3) better-than-expected operating margin improvement (e.g., due to scale advantage from the Fab-Lite model).
Downside risks: (1) slower-than-expected recovery in the smartphone market, (2) intensified market competition from domestic players, and (3) major failure in the R&D of new RF modules.

We derive our PO of Rmb251 on discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation approach, with a weighted-average cost of capital (WACC) of 9% and terminal growth rate of 3%, implying 57x FY27E P/E, which is largely in line with the average valuation of China A-share fabless.
Upside risks: 1) faster-than-expected launch of PCIe Switch new products, 2) higher-than-expected revenue contribution from PCIe Retimer, and 3) faster-than-expected MRCD/MDB industry penetration.
Downside risks: 1) intensified competition from peers or potential newcomers, 2) geopolitical risks on trade restrictions (AI Chips), and 3) delayed launch of new CPUs by others.

Our PO of Rmb47 is based on 32x 2H26-1H27E P/E, which is set 15% discount to the average valuation of China power semiconductor companies due to its smaller revenue scale. We think that this valuation is justified by NCE Power's strong earnings growth momentum of 25% CAGR in FY25-28E, driven by solid top-line growth on continued share gain by launching more high-end products.

Upside risks: (1) stronger-than-expected demand for power devices (i.e., auto), (2) launch of new products with technological advancements (e.g., SiC / power modules), and (3) better-than-expected margins improvement.

Downside risks: (1) supply chain disruption, (2) intensified competition of China power semiconductor market, (3) failure to catch up with technology advancement (e.g., SiC and GaN), and (4) regulatory challenges.

Our PO of Rmb235 is based on 60x 12mths forward P/E, which is set in-line with the average of China fabless peers listed in A-share. We think our target valuation multiple is not demanding given that 1) it is 0.5SD below its historical average of c.90x and 2) encouraging growth outlook with 39% earnings CAGR in FY25-27E. We use a P/E-based valuation methodology to better factor in its earnings growth outlook.
Upside risks: 1) faster edge-AI computing penetration, 2) more design wins, 3) automotive and robotics market expansion, and 4) faster semi localization trends.
Downside risks: 1) downstream demand volatility, 2) competitive pressure, 3) technology transition risk with slower new product launch, and 4) supply chain and geopolitical risks.

Our price objective (PO) of RMB73 is based on discounted cash flow (DCF) methodology, which incorporates 8.7% weighted-average cost of capital (WACC) and 3% terminal growth rate, and is supported by 1) sound balance sheet (40-50% net cash), and 2) recovering operating cash flow generation along with higher revenue base.

Upside risks: (1) quicker adoption of ultrasonic fingerprint solutions by clients, (2) faster-than-expected ramp-up of emerging products, and (3) quicker addressable market expansion in non-smartphone business.
Downside risks: (1) faster-than-expected product ASP erosion from intensified competition, (2) weaker-than-expected smartphone shipment, (3) wider adoption of non-fingerprint biometric sensors.
